correctness.rationale: Every mixed falling-factorial probability is counted exactly. Equation (7) isolates the unique order \(n^{-1/2}\) correction from repeated-symbol matches, controls all higher powers by \(O(n^{-1})\), and factorial majorants permit summation on fixed complex disks. Cauchy yields an \(\ell^1\) error \(O(n^{-1})\) for the entire probability mass function. The Poisson second-difference sign factor and its telescoping mass at mean two give \(5e^{-2}/3\). Exact finite enumeration and rational moment checking passed; no finite test was used to infer infinity.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper explicitly singled out multiplicity \(\lceil\sqrt n\rceil\) as its borderline example and left a logarithmic gap between general Poisson upper and lower rates. This result closes that gap quantitatively with an exact nonzero constant for the intrinsic critical profile and, structurally, a signed whole-distribution first correction for every positive fixed critical-scale constant. The precise statistic is a natural matching count; the result is neither arbitrary finite slicing nor a routine restatement of a known inequality.
